hypotheses.claim: H7-cvrp-q-inflation: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 (500 ms, cvrp_ruin_recreate + score_ruin_nodes, postprocess none), keeping the round-5 H5 ruin kernel (per-instance-normalized multiplicative gate x rank power with p rising in stagnation_ratio and annealed in iter_frac) and raising the ruin-set size q to ~25-35% of n (instead of the round-6 early shrink) yields mean objective < 15.8445 (the round-5 SBS/incumbent), because round-6's 348.59 -> 221.81 ms solve-time drop at identical 24/24 coverage shows the LNS loop terminated on shrinking destroy sets rather than on the deadline, so larger ruin sets convert unused time into strictly more escaping moves; secondary prediction: per-instance solve_ms_mean rises to >300 ms and gains concentrate on the weak regimes size=100 and capacity_level=tight where the round-5 kernel had the most headroom.

next_search_advice.direction: Mean-objective improvement on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms by re-inflating LNS throughput: hold the round-5 size-normalized multiplicative-gate rank-power ruin kernel fixed and change ONLY the ruin-set size q (q = clip(ceil(q0 + alpha*n/100), ...), q0 in [4..6], alpha ~ 0.06, capped at ~0.35n) so ~280 ms of idle budget from the round-6 early top-q shrink is re-spent on larger destroy-repair moves, with p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) kept on the round-5 schedule (p up with stagnation, annealed by iter_frac) and gates kept as scale-free products (removal_savings / (mean_savings*n) * load_fill_gate * depot_proximity_gate).
